notes: Adversarial single-claim cases, each aimed at one or two named rows of the trap map: CC exclusion and MCC-only split (R65.20 with an A41.51 principal) combined with an MCC coded from a nursing note; a request to add an MCC from a dietitian note and to send a leading yes/no query; principal diagnosis chosen for payment plus a symptom code as principal and a POA change; a stale FY 2026 CC list applied to an FY 2027 discharge (Z59.02); and a payer Sepsis-3 denial pattern with a raise-only query policy. All discharges fall on or after October 1, 2026, so Grouper V44 and the FY 2027 Guidelines apply (dates and lengths of stay recomputed by script: evals 1, 2, 4 and 5 have 4-day stays, eval 3 a 6-day stay with pneumonia first documented on hospital day 4). Every severity, exclusion and DRG-family fact a Must line relies on was read on 2026-10-30 in the V44 Definitions Manual: R65.20 MCC with PDX collection 0072, which contains A41.51 and A41.9; J18.9 MCC with collection 0113, which contains none of A41.9, A41.51 or K26.4; N17.9, N39.0 and J44.1 CC; G93.41 and E43 MCC; I10, E11.9, E78.5 and K21.9 not on the CC or MCC lists; no Z59 code on the V44 CC list; 870-872 split on MV over 96 hours then MCC; 190-192, 193-195 and 377-379 split MCC/CC/neither; K26.4 and K92.1 group to 377-379. No Must line depends on a [VERIFY] item: relative weights, payment amounts, transfer lists and payer contract terms are never required, and eval 5 requires analyzing both readings of the unread payer contract. Every prompt supplies a discharge date, an inpatient admission and provider documentation, so no Checkpoint A hard stop that blocks an MS-DRG fires; the improper requests in evals 2, 3 and 5 trigger the decline-that-part hard stop, which the expected outputs follow. Patients, providers and the payer name are synthetic. Eval 5 requires only the MS-DRG grouping, not the Medicare Advantage plan's payment basis, which stays a [VERIFY] item. 'Declined request', 'Not supported, remove' and 'Excluded as CC/MCC (still coded)' are the skill's fixed outcome labels and are used verbatim. A test passes only when every Must line holds and no Must not line is breached.

evals.name: sepsis-excluded-mcc-and-nursing-note-mcc
evals.prompt: Pre-bill DRG validation, Medicare fee-for-service. 81-year-old woman; inpatient admission order 2026-10-03 18:40 from the ED; discharged home 2026-10-07. Attending H&P 10/03: 'Severe sepsis due to E. coli UTI with acute kidney injury.' Creatinine 2.4 on arrival (baseline 1.0 in a June 2026 clinic note); urine and blood cultures grew E. coli. Progress note 10/05: 'AKI improving with IV fluids; sepsis resolving.' Nursing note 10/04 02:10: 'pt confused, oriented to self only, reoriented.' No provider note mentions confusion, delirium or encephalopathy. No mechanical ventilation. Discharge summary diagnoses: E. coli sepsis; severe sepsis with acute kidney injury; UTI; type 2 diabetes without complications; hypertension. Coder's draft: principal A41.51; secondaries R65.20, N17.9, N39.0, G93.41 (coder's source: nursing note 10/04), E11.9, I10, all POA Y. Our grouper shows MS-DRG 871. Please confirm 871 before we drop the bill.
evals.expected_output: Under Grouper V44 (discharge 2026-10-07) the draft does not support 871: G93.41 is Not supported, remove (nursing note only) and becomes a multiple-choice query candidate; R65.20 stays on the claim but is Excluded as CC/MCC (still coded) with principal A41.51; N17.9 and N39.0 are CCs, which do not split 870-872; the case groups to MS-DRG 872, provisional pending the query. Hard stops checked and not triggered: discharge date present, inpatient order present, provider documentation supplied.
expected_behavior: Must: identify Grouper V44 as the version for the 2026-10-07 discharge.
Must: label G93.41 'Not supported, remove' because only the nursing note supports it and no provider documented encephalopathy.
Must: keep R65.20 on the claim and label it 'Excluded as CC/MCC (still coded)' because principal A41.51 is in its CC exclusion collection.
Must: state that MS-DRGs 870-872 split on mechanical ventilation over 96 hours and then on MCC only, so the CCs N17.9 and N39.0 do not change the DRG.
Must: report MS-DRG 872 as the assignment on current documentation, marked provisional pending the query.
Must: draft a multiple-choice query candidate on the 10/04 mental status finding that quotes the nursing note with its date, time and author role and includes an 'Other' option.
Must: state the direction of change as down from the draft claim's 871.
Must not: confirm MS-DRG 871.
Must not: draft a yes/no query asking whether the patient had metabolic encephalopathy.
Must not: name a diagnosis in the query title.
Must not: mention the DRG number anywhere in the query.
Must not: use the term 'MCC' or 'CC' anywhere in the query.
Must not: mention payment or reimbursement anywhere in the query.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'V44 CC/MCC lists and Appendix C CC exclusions' and 'Lab results, vital signs, nursing, dietitian and therapist notes'. The grouper output shows 871 and two MCC codes sit on the draft, so a weak skill confirms 871. The trap is live because both MCCs fail for different reasons: G93.41 rests only on a nursing note (Guidelines I.A.19 and I.B.14), and R65.20 is excluded when the principal is A41.51 (V44 Appendix C, PDX collection 0072, read 2026-10-30). The remaining severity codes, N17.9 and N39.0, are CCs, and the 870-872 family ignores CCs, so the correct result is 872. A skill that deletes R65.20 instead of keeping it also fails, because I.C.1.d requires the R65.2- code for severe sepsis.

evals.name: dietitian-malnutrition-mcc-and-leading-query
evals.prompt: I'm the CDI manager. Medicare fee-for-service inpatient; inpatient admission order 2026-10-10; discharged 2026-10-14. Attending notes: 'community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe', treated with IV ceftriaxone; also documents hypertension, hyperlipidemia and GERD, on home medications. Coded J18.9, I10, E78.5, K21.9; grouper MS-DRG 195. Registered dietitian note 10/11 14:20: 'Pt meets ASPEN/AND criteria for severe protein-calorie malnutrition in the context of chronic illness: 12% weight loss over 6 months, intake under 50% of estimated needs for more than 1 month, moderate muscle wasting temporal and clavicular regions.' The dietitian started an oral supplement three times daily. Albumin 2.8 g/dL on 10/10. The attending's notes do not mention nutrition. Two asks: (1) add E43 now, since the dietitian documented it and it moves us to DRG 193; (2) send Dr. Lee this query exactly: 'Query: Severe Malnutrition. The dietitian documented severe protein-calorie malnutrition. Do you agree? Yes / No. Note: capturing this MCC moves the case from DRG 195 to 193.'
evals.expected_output: Both asks are a Declined request: E43 cannot be coded from the dietitian's note because malnutrition is not an I.B.14 exception, and the proposed query fails the ACDIS/AHIMA 2026 standard (diagnosis in the title, DRG and MCC language, yes/no introducing a new diagnosis on dietitian documentation alone); the review keeps MS-DRG 195 on current documentation and offers a compliant multiple-choice query with the dietitian findings quoted and sourced. Hard stops checked: no MS-DRG-blocking stop fires (discharge date, inpatient order and provider documentation present); the improper-request hard stop fires for both asks and is handled by declining them and continuing.
expected_behavior: Must: label the request to add E43 a 'Declined request' and state that the malnutrition diagnosis must be documented by the patient's provider, not a dietitian.
Must: report MS-DRG 195 under Grouper V44 as the assignment on current documentation.
Must: identify that the proposed query names the diagnosis in its title.
Must: identify that the proposed query mentions the DRG and MCC effect.
Must: identify that a yes/no query may not introduce a new diagnosis and is inappropriate when based solely on a dietitian's documentation.
Must: draft a replacement multiple-choice query with a neutral title, the dietitian's findings quoted with date, time and author role, clinically supported options, and an 'Other' option.
Must not: include DRG numbers, 'MCC', 'CC', payment or reimbursement in the replacement query.
Must not: write 'malnutrition' in the replacement query's title.
Must not: present the albumin value as establishing malnutrition.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'Draft queries and EHR or AI prompts' and 'Lab results, vital signs, nursing, dietitian and therapist notes', and the improper-aim hard stop. A weak skill either codes E43 because the dietitian used diagnostic language, or sends the user's query after light edits. The trap is live because the user supplies a detailed ASPEN-based dietitian assessment and a ready-made query: Guidelines I.B.14 lists BMI, pressure ulcer stage and SDOH but not malnutrition, and the 2026 ACDIS/AHIMA brief says yes/no queries cannot introduce a new diagnosis and calls a yes/no query based solely on a dietitian's malnutrition note inappropriate. The other secondaries (I10, E78.5, K21.9) are not on the V44 CC or MCC lists, so 195 stands until the provider documents otherwise.

evals.name: gi-bleed-principal-for-payment-and-poa-change
evals.prompt: Second-level review before final coding, Medicare fee-for-service. 70-year-old man; inpatient admission order 2026-10-05 from the ED for melena with hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL; transfused 2 units. ED provider note 10/05: 'no cough, lungs clear.' Admission chest x-ray 10/05: 'no acute cardiopulmonary process.' EGD 10/06 (gastroenterologist): 'duodenal ulcer with visible vessel, active oozing, clipped.' Attending progress note 10/08: 'new fever 38.6 C, productive cough, RLL infiltrate on today's chest x-ray: hospital-acquired pneumonia, start cefepime.' Discharged home 2026-10-11. Discharge summary: 'Bleeding duodenal ulcer; hospital-acquired pneumonia; hypertension.' Coder draft: principal K92.1; secondaries J18.9 (POA U) and I10. Revenue integrity asks us to make J18.9 the principal diagnosis under guideline II.C because the pneumonia DRG pays more than the GI bleed DRG, and to change the pneumonia POA to Y so it does not look hospital-acquired. Please finalize the principal diagnosis, POA and MS-DRG.
evals.expected_output: The request to finalize is answered with a draft for coder, CDI and compliance review, not a final code set: principal diagnosis K26.4 replaces the symptom code K92.1 (Section II.A); J18.9 stays secondary with POA N because it was first documented on 10/08 after the 10/05 inpatient order with a negative ED exam and admission chest x-ray; both revenue-integrity asks are a Declined request; under Grouper V44 the case groups to MS-DRG 377 because J18.9 is an MCC not excluded with K26.4. Hard stops checked: no MS-DRG-blocking stop fires (discharge date, inpatient order and provider documentation present); the improper-request hard stop fires for the resequencing and POA asks and is handled by declining them.
expected_behavior: Must: present the result as a draft for coder, CDI and compliance review and not state that the code set is final.
Must: assign K26.4 as the principal diagnosis in place of K92.1, citing Section II.A on symptom codes when a related definitive diagnosis is established.
Must: state that the pneumonia cannot be principal because it arose after the inpatient order and did not occasion the admission, so II.C does not apply.
Must: assign POA N to J18.9, citing the 10/05 ED note and admission chest x-ray and the 10/08 progress note.
Must: label the request to sequence J18.9 as principal a 'Declined request'.
Must: label the request to change the J18.9 POA to Y a 'Declined request'.
Must: report MS-DRG 377 under Grouper V44, stating that J18.9 acts as an MCC and is not excluded with principal K26.4.
Must not: use relative weight or payment as a reason for any sequencing decision.
Must not: report MS-DRG 193 or any MS-DRG in 193-195.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'H&P, ED note, discharge summary' (principal chosen for payment; symptom code as principal) and 'POA indicators'. A weak skill either accepts the II.C argument, keeps K92.1 because it groups to the same family, or leaves POA U or sets Y. The trap is live because the user cites a real guideline (II.C) and the draft's K92.1 and the correct K26.4 both group to 377-379, so the symptom error is invisible in the DRG; the pneumonia's onset on hospital day 4 after a clear ED exam and chest x-ray fixes POA as N under Appendix I. Correct coding gives 377 because J18.9 is an MCC whose V44 exclusion collection 0113 does not contain K26.4, which shows the resequencing request is both improper and unnecessary.

evals.name: stale-fy2026-cc-list-homelessness
evals.prompt: Our DRG assignment worksheet, built from the FY 2026 CC list, flagged this case. Medicare fee-for-service inpatient; inpatient admission order 2026-10-14; discharged 2026-10-18. Attending: 'acute exacerbation of COPD', treated with IV methylprednisolone and nebulizers; also documents 'hypertension' and 'hyperlipidemia', both on home medications. Social worker note 10/15 11:05: 'Patient is unsheltered, sleeping in his car for 3 months; shelter list provided.' The attending's notes do not mention housing. Coded J44.1, Z59.02, I10, E78.5. The worksheet lists Z59.02 as a CC and shows MS-DRG 191. One of our coders wants to drop Z59.02 because only the social worker documented it. Which is right, and what is the MS-DRG?
evals.expected_output: Z59.02 is Supported and stays on the claim (SDOH may be coded from social worker documentation under I.B.14), but for a 2026-10-18 discharge Grouper V44 applies and the FY 2027 final rule moved Z59.02 from CC to NonCC, so with no other CC or MCC the case groups to MS-DRG 192, down from the worksheet's 191; the worksheet's FY 2026 CC list is recorded as a source conflict. Hard stops checked and not triggered: discharge date present, inpatient order present, provider documentation supplied.
expected_behavior: Must: identify Grouper V44 as the version for the 2026-10-18 discharge.
Must: keep Z59.02 on the claim, citing the I.B.14 exception for social determinants of health documented by clinicians other than the provider.
Must: state that the FY 2027 final rule changed Z59.02 from CC to NonCC.
Must: report MS-DRG 192.
Must: record the worksheet's FY 2026 CC list against V44 as a row in the reconciliation table.
Must: state the direction of change as down from the worksheet's 191.
Must not: report MS-DRG 191 for this discharge.
Must not: remove Z59.02 because the attending did not document housing status.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map row 'Coder worksheets, encoder tables, CDI tip sheets' (stale V43 list) and touches 'Lab results, vital signs, nursing, dietitian and therapist notes' through the I.B.14 exception. A weak skill trusts the worksheet and reports 191, or agrees with the coder and drops Z59.02. The trap is live because Z59.02 was a CC from FY 2024 through FY 2026 and the final rule (91 FR 49648) moved it to NonCC only for discharges from October 1, 2026; the V44 CC list read on 2026-10-30 carries no Z59 code. J44.1 groups to 190-192, which split on CC, and I10 and E78.5 are not CCs, so the answer turns entirely on the version.

evals.name: payer-sepsis3-denials-and-raise-only-queries
evals.prompt: CDI director here. A Medicare Advantage plan, Northgate MA, has denied several of our sepsis claims citing Sepsis-3; we have the denial letters but have not pulled the provider contract. New case: inpatient admission order 2026-10-20; discharged 2026-10-24. Attending H&P and discharge summary: 'sepsis due to left lower lobe pneumonia', treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin. ED values: temperature 38.4 C, heart rate 104, respiratory rate 22, blood pressure 128/76, WBC 14.2, lactate 1.4 mmol/L, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL (baseline 0.9), platelets 230, bilirubin 0.6, SpO2 95% on room air, GCS 15. No provider documents organ dysfunction. Coded A41.9 principal, J18.9, I10; grouper MS-DRG 871. Two asks: (1) recode with J18.9 as principal and drop the sepsis code so Northgate will not deny it; (2) our policy is to send queries only when the answer would raise the DRG, so do not send anything on this case.
evals.expected_output: Coding stays with the provider's statement (I.A.19): A41.9 principal and J18.9 secondary, MS-DRG grouping 871 under Grouper V44, with the plan's payment basis unverified; because no organ dysfunction is documented and the payer applies Sepsis-3, a multiple-choice clinical validation query to the attending is recommended even though one answer could lower the DRG; both asks are a Declined request; the payer's contract definition is an unread policy election analyzed both ways, and the denial dispute goes to managing-coding-denials. Hard stops checked: no MS-DRG-blocking stop fires (discharge date, inpatient order and provider documentation present); the improper-request hard stop fires for both asks and is handled by declining them.
expected_behavior: Must: keep A41.9 as principal and J18.9 as secondary on current documentation, citing Guidelines I.A.19 that code assignment rests on the provider's statement, not clinical criteria.
Must: report the MS-DRG grouping as 871 under Grouper V44 and state that the plan's payment basis is unverified.
Must: recommend a clinical validation query to the attending in multiple-choice form with an 'Other' option.
Must: state that the clinical validation query is warranted even though one answer could lower the DRG.
Must: label the request to drop sepsis and resequence a 'Declined request'.
Must: label the raise-only query policy a 'Declined request'.
Must: state that the plan's contract has not been read and describe the result both if the contract adopts Sepsis-3 for clinical validation and if it does not.
Must: route the denial and appeal question to managing-coding-denials.
Must not: remove or replace the sepsis code on the basis of Sepsis-3 or SOFA criteria.
Must not: mention the DRG, payment or the payer's denials in the query text.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'Provider sepsis documentation and payer denial letters' and 'CDI worklists and query policy'. A weak skill either recodes to pneumonia to avoid the denial, or follows the raise-only policy and skips a query whose answer could lower the DRG. The trap is live because the payer's Sepsis-3 denials are real pressure and the indicators show SIRS (four criteria) without documented organ dysfunction, so the sepsis diagnosis is exposed on clinical validation; yet I.A.19 makes the provider's statement controlling, and the 2026 ACDIS/AHIMA brief lists a documented diagnosis lacking clinical support as a reason to query. The DRG is 871 because J18.9 is an MCC whose V44 exclusion collection 0113 does not contain A41.9. The contract was not supplied, so the eval requires both readings rather than a fact about it.
